text:
Kevin T.: Heads-up — we need to finalize PII redaction + sampling for request/response logs before Dedicated deploy next week. Biggest worry: low-volume customers and rare PII leaks.
Marta P.: +1. We still haven’t decided between conservative redaction (drop entire fields) vs token-level masking. Tradeoffs: recoverability for debugging vs risk of leakage.
Samir: for infra ops, conservative is simpler. If we mask tokens we need deterministic hashing + salt per-customer. Ops would like an escape hatch for on-call.
Anna L.: escape hatch is the tricky bit re: compliance. Audit trail must show who enabled unredacted capture and for how long. Also we have to show approval metadata in the console.
Kevin T.: Agreed. Proposal: default sampling 1% for request+response bodies, 100% for headers/metadata (non-body), but redact any JSON keys matching name/email/ssn using regex. On-call can escalate to 100% for a rolling 30m window with audit entry. Thoughts?
Marta P.: sounds OK but we need per-customer overrides and bucketed sampling because some customers are tiny — 1% might be 0 events. For customers with <100 requests/day, we should floor to at least 5 samples/day if they opt-in to debug mode.
Samir: +1 on floor. Also we should consider sampling by route severity: errors and latency outliers should be sampled at higher rate automatically.
Anna L.: UX: in the Console rollout, show "logging controls" at project level with toggles: default sampling, debug window, manual snapshot. Manual snapshot triggers one immediate full capture (still redacted unless customer grants dev-consent).
Kevin T.: here's a draft of the sampling config we could implement in the router. Critique please:
```yaml
sampling:
  default_rate: 0.01  # 1%
  min_daily_per_customer: 5
  error_rate_override: 1.0  # full capture on 5xx or latency>2s
  per_customer_overrides:
    - id: "partner_omega"
      rate: 1.0
  debug_window_minutes: 30
  debug_audit_label: "oncall_manual_capture"
  redact_keys_regex: "(?i)\b(name|email|ssn|credit_card)\b"
```
Marta P.: regex is fine but needs testing against nested JSON and arrays. Also add specific handling for embeddings/attachments — they're large and should not be stored even redacted.
Samir: telemetry-bot just reported an SLO alert pattern; we can tie sampling to anomaly detection too. If anomaly score>threshold, bump sampling for 1h.
telemetry-bot: [system] anomaly_watch triggered for route "/v1/generate" (score=0.87). Suggested sampling bump to 50% for 60 minutes.
Anna L.: ok include anomaly-based bump. We should also make the policy composable: base_rate -> overrides (customer, error, anomaly, manual) -> final_rate, with explicit precedence rules in docs.
Kevin T.: security question: can redaction run in the router (edge) or only in central logging pipeline? Running at edge is safer (never send raw) but increases CPU cost on GPUs/edge nodes. Thoughts?
Marta P.: prefer edge redaction for compliance; if cost too high we can do client-side SDK masking for known PII keys and server-side fallback.
Samir: ops: implement edge redaction with a small whitelist of keys we allow to keep unredacted (request_id, route, latency) and then pipe the redacted body to Kafka. We'll prototype with a Rust library.
Kevin T.: one more operational constraint: retention. How long do we keep sampled traces? Compliance might want 90 days, but storage cost will blow up. Proposal: 30d default, 90d on request with legal hold + enterprise package.
Anna L.: include ability to purge per-customer on request, and an audit log entry for purge actions. Also limit exports: exported logs should be redacted unless explicit opt-in.
Marta P.: regarding console UI, show an estimated cost slider when customers change sampling ("estimated monthly storage delta: $X").
Samir: sounds great. Implementation plan: 1) land config schema + regex engine tests, 2) implement edge redaction + sampling router, 3) console controls + audit trails, 4) canary on Dedicated region, 5) post-launch metric dashboards.
Kevin T.: OK assigning owners: Marta -> console/UX + policy docs; Samir -> edge implementation + ops integration; Anna -> compliance + audit logging; Kevin -> overall spec + rollout plan.
Ops SRE: FYI will schedule canary on friday morning 09:00 PST, tagging the deploy with `canary/pii-sample-v1`. Will post results.
Marta P.: I'll draft the policy doc and add example RGs and tests. Ping me if you have edge-case examples (attachments, base64 blobs, long embeddings).
Samir: I'll add fuzz tests for regex and nested objects.
Kevin T.: thanks team. If no objections by EOD we'll ship the spec to the RFC repo. :thumbsup:
